risk_architecture.name: Structural exposure and loss architecture, shared identically by all three Attempt 2 candidates
risk_architecture.why_shared: Declaring one architecture once, identically across candidates, means its degrees of freedom are counted once rather than three times. If RA1 were tuned per candidate, three candidates would carry three independent sets of risk parameters and the search would be three times wider than it appears.
risk_architecture.design_intent: S3-C2 is satisfied if and only if the constitution section 5.1 research shutdown never fires. RA1 is the structural answer to that: it lowers exposure, caps single-position loss, reduces size as account drawdown grows, and bounds time at risk. Every constant below is either taken from a frozen artifact or derived arithmetically from constants that are, and none was selected by inspecting an Attempt 1 equity path.
risk_architecture.prohibition_on_mechanical_targeting: RA1 is not a device for stopping at 14.99%. No rule references the 15% ceiling, no rule references a drawdown level between 10% and 15%, and no rule is conditioned on proximity to the shutdown. The deepest level RA1 reacts to is 10%, which is the constitution's own section 5.2 hard risk halt, declared for live trading and adopted here as a research-side de-risking trigger.

RA1-1.name: Exposure ceiling
RA1-1.rule: f_base = 0.50. No entry may request a budget above f_base multiplied by account equity measured at the decision close.
RA1-1.derivation: Not fitted. The constitution's section 5.2 live soft risk halt is 8% below the high-water mark and its hard risk halt is 10%. RA1-3 caps a single position's nominal decline at L = 0.08. With f_base = 0.50 the worst nominal single-position cost to the account is f_base * L = 0.040, which is half the soft-halt distance and 40% of the hard-halt distance. No single position can, at its declared limit, carry the account through a halt rung on its own.
RA1-1.relation_to_constitutional_cap: The constitution section 3 ceiling is 95% gross exposure with a 5% minimum cash buffer, and the sealed cost model enforces it. RA1-1 requests less. It never requests more and cannot.
RA1-1.defensive_leg_note: RA1-1 applies uniformly, including to a defensive Treasury leg. A candidate holding SHY therefore holds about 50% SHY and about 50% cash, which reduces the defensive leg's return contribution relative to Attempt 1's F6. This is a disclosed cost of the architecture, not an oversight. No instrument-specific carve-out is granted, because a per-instrument exposure exemption would be a discretionary rule and the whole point of RA1 is that its rules are not discretionary.

RA1-2.name: Volatility-targeted entry sizing
RA1-2.entry_only_reason: The sealed portfolio accounting appends a closed trade only when a position is fully closed, so a position is all-or-nothing. Re-sizing an open position would require a partial exit the accounting does not model. Sizing is therefore decided once, at entry, and never adjusted while the position is open.
rule: sigma_target = 0.10, annualised.
sigma = VOL20 of the symbol being entered, measured at the decision close.
f_vol = sigma_target / sigma.
f_cap = the RA1-5 ladder value for the decision session.
f = min(f_cap, f_vol).
If sigma == 0: no entry, reason NO_ENTRY_ZERO_VOLATILITY.
If f < f_floor = 0.05: no entry that session, reason NO_ENTRY_VOLATILITY_FLOOR.
budget = f * equity at the decision close.
If budget < min_order_notional_usd = 1.00 from SE100-CFG-2001 sizing: no entry, reason NO_ENTRY_SIZE_FLOOR.
Otherwise emit BUY with that budget. The engine applies its own exposure cap, cash buffer, one-cent budget safety margin, and share rounding on top, and may reduce the executed notional further.
RA1-2.sigma_target_rationale: 0.10 annualised is a deliberately low volatility target: below the long-run realised volatility of every equity ETF in the frozen universe, so the target binds rather than decorates, and above zero by enough that a position of economically meaningful size is still taken in calm regimes. It is one round number declared once and probed by a neighbour at 0.08 in every candidate.
RA1-2.f_floor_rationale: f_floor = 0.05 mirrors the constitution's 5% minimum cash buffer read as a smallest-meaningful-fraction. It is a safety rail against an absurdly small position in an extreme volatility regime, not a filter: it binds only when sigma exceeds sigma_target / f_floor = 2.00, that is 200% annualised, which is far above any level the frozen universe has exhibited. Declared so that the case is decided in advance rather than on sight.
RA1-2.cannot_increase_exposure: f = min(f_cap, f_vol), so volatility targeting can only reduce exposure below the RA1-1 ceiling. It can never raise it.

RA1-3.name: Per-position loss control
rule: P_ref = close of the DECISION session on which the entry order was scheduled.
On any later decision session t at which the symbol is in context.open_symbols: if close(symbol, t) <= P_ref * (1 - L), emit a full exit, reason EXIT_LOSS_CONTROL.
A pending P_ref is discarded if the symbol is absent from context.open_symbols at the next decision session, because the entry was not filled.
RA1-3.why_decision_close_and_not_fill_price: The fill price is the next session's open and is not exposed to the candidate at decision time. Referencing the decision close keeps the rule computable from information the candidate is allowed to see, and structurally prevents a look-ahead read of the fill. The difference between the decision close and the fill open is one overnight gap and is disclosed as such rather than modelled away.
RA1-3.L_rationale: 0.08 is the constitution's own section 5.2 live soft risk halt distance, adopted at the position level. Taking the number from a frozen artifact rather than choosing one keeps it out of the search space.
RA1-3.not_a_stop_order: This is a close-referenced exit that fills at the next open under MARKET_ON_NEXT_OPEN. It is not a stop order, not a stop-limit, and not an intraday trigger. The project holds no intraday data, so no intraday trigger could be evaluated.
RA1-3.not_a_bound: RA1-3 does not bound loss at 8%. The trigger is evaluated at a close and filled at the next open, so one overnight gap and one session of exposure sit between the trigger and the exit. Constitution section 5.2: 'Stops are risk tools, not guarantees; overnight gaps may exceed intended losses.' A position that declines faster than the rule can react loses more than L, and the account loses f times that larger amount.

RA1-4.name: Maximum holding period
rule: H is declared per candidate.
sessions_held counts the decision sessions on which the symbol has appeared in context.open_symbols, the current session included.
If sessions_held >= H, emit a full exit, reason EXIT_MAX_HOLD.
RA1-4.purpose: Bounds time at risk and forces every thesis to be re-underwritten. A position that has not resolved within its candidate's declared horizon is closed rather than held indefinitely.
RA1-4.per_candidate_H_is_not_a_trade_count_dia: Each H is set from its candidate's own stated thesis horizon, and in every case H is longer than the horizon the thesis names, so H is the outer bound rather than the operative exit. The values are stated with their reasoning in each candidate block and are not adjusted to reach any gate threshold.

RA1-5.name: Account de-risk ladder
RA1-5.read: at entry only, to set f_cap for the RA1-2 computation
rule: hwm is the running maximum of context.equity over the decision sessions of the run, seeded at the first decision session's equity and updated on every decision session whether the account is flat or not.
dd = (hwm - equity) / hwm at the decision close.
RA1-5.equity_series_identity: context.equity is the same value the engine records before it evaluates the section 5.1 shutdown, so RA1-5's drawdown series is byte-identical to the shutdown's own. The ladder and the shutdown read one series, not two approximations of one.
RA1-5.never_blocks_entry: The ladder reduces size. It never blocks an entry and never sets f_cap to zero. This is deliberate and is the correction of a rejected earlier formulation.
RA1-5.rejected_alternative: An earlier formulation blocked new entries once dd reached 0.08 until equity recovered above the high-water mark. It is recorded here because it is fatally defective and the defect is instructive: a flat account's equity is constant, so equity can never recover, so the block can never re-arm. That rule would produce a permanently dead strategy - which is the failure mode the constitution's own shutdown already represents, reintroduced by the risk overlay meant to avoid it. It is also what the operating constraint against making a strategy incapable of meaningful trading solely to suppress drawdown forbids.
RA1-5.rung_rationale: 0.08 and 0.10 are the constitution's section 5.2 live soft and hard risk halt distances, verbatim. The multipliers halve and then halve again. Nothing here is a new number chosen by the researcher except the choice to halve, which is declared and is probed indirectly by the f_base neighbour in every candidate.

RA1-6.name: Re-entry rule after a risk exit
RA1-6.rule: After an exit with reason EXIT_LOSS_CONTROL or EXIT_MAX_HOLD, the candidate may not re-enter that same symbol for R = 5 decision sessions counted from the decision session that scheduled the exit. A blocked entry is recorded with reason NO_ENTRY_LOCKOUT. An exit with reason EXIT_SIGNAL creates no lockout.
RA1-6.R_rationale: One exchange week. A cooling-off period after a risk-driven exit prevents the loss control from converting a single adverse move into an immediate sequence of identical entries into the same condition. Five sessions is the shortest period that spans a full weekly cycle.
RA1-6.rejected_alternative: The lockout was first specified as lasting until the candidate's entry condition evaluated false at least once. That is defective for the same reason as the rejected RA1-5 formulation: a regime condition can remain true for years, so the lockout could fail to expire and would leave the account in cash indefinitely. A fixed number of sessions always expires.
RA1-6.not_load_bearing_for_the_drawdown_arithm: The drawdown arithmetic below assumes back-to-back maximum losses with no lockout at all, so RA1-6 can only improve on it. It is an economic sensibility rule, not part of the bound.

RA1-7.name: Conflict resolution
RA1-7.rule: The shared flat_first_rule, adopted unchanged. A candidate never schedules an exit and an entry for the same fill session, so every symbol switch costs one full session out of the market. Combined with RA1-6, a switch that follows a risk exit costs at least six sessions out of the market.

RA1-8.name: All-or-nothing positions
RA1-8.rule: Entries and exits are for the full position. No partial entry, no partial exit, no scaling in, no scaling out, no averaging down, no pyramiding.
RA1-8.reason: Constitution section 5.1 prohibits averaging down without an explicit predeclared rule, and the sealed portfolio accounting appends a closed trade only when a position is fully closed. Partial exits would make the closed-trade series - the basis of S3-C3, S3-C4, S3-C5, and S3-C6 - ambiguous.

exit_precedence.rule: At most one exit is emitted per session because positions are all-or-nothing. When more than one exit condition is true on the same decision session, the position is closed once and the attributed reason is the highest-precedence condition in the order above.
exit_precedence.purpose: Reason attribution only. The precedence changes no exit decision - the position closes either way - so it cannot affect any metric. It exists so that the evidence can report how many exits each mechanism caused, which is how RA1-3 and RA1-4 are diagnosed instead of being probed by a neighbour.

engine_shutdown_relationship.enforcement: The section 5.1 research shutdown is enforced by the engine for every run, primary and neighbour and stressed alike. It is not disabled, not relaxed, and not treated as an artefact.
engine_shutdown_relationship.candidate_behaviour: A candidate emits no order on any decision session where context.shutdown_active is true. This is belt-and-braces; the engine already forces liquidation and blocks entries.
engine_shutdown_relationship.no_candidate_reads_the_ceiling: No RA1 rule and no candidate rule references 0.15, the shutdown state, or the distance to it as an input to sizing or signalling.

drawdown_arithmetic.claim: This is an arithmetic property of the declared constants, computed by hand from RA1-1, RA1-3, and RA1-5 before any Attempt 2 code exists. It is NOT a prediction, NOT a guarantee, and NOT a claim that S3-C2 will be met.
drawdown_arithmetic.worst_case_sequence: Consecutive round trips each losing exactly the RA1-3 limit, starting from the high-water mark with equity 1.0. Loss per trade = f_cap * L.
steps: trade 1: dd = 0.0000, f_cap = 0.500, loss 4.000%, equity 0.960000, dd after = 4.0000%
trade 7: dd = 14.1541%, f_cap = 0.125, loss 1.000%, equity 0.849874, dd after = 15.0126% - BREACH
drawdown_arithmetic.result: Seven consecutive maximum-loss round trips are required to breach the 15% ceiling. Six leave drawdown at 14.15%.
drawdown_arithmetic.middle_rung_note: The 0.25 rung is skipped on this particular path, because trade 3 carries drawdown from 7.84% straight to 11.53%. The middle rung is reached by paths made of smaller individual losses, not by the maximum-loss path.
caveats: RA1-3 is not a bound. The trigger is a close and the fill is the next open, so a gap can exceed L and the per-trade loss can exceed f_cap * L. Constitution section 5.2 says so in terms.
A position that declines without ever printing a close at or below the trigger, then gaps through it, loses more than L.

Drawdown is measured at session closes because the project holds no intraday data. Every measured drawdown is a lower bound on the true intraday figure, and this is an Attempt 1 limitation that Attempt 2 inherits unchanged.

Losses need not be consecutive. Interleaved gains raise the high-water mark and reset the ladder, which helps; interleaved small losses can walk the account down through the rungs more slowly than this path, which does not.

This arithmetic says nothing about profitability. A structure that never breaches the ceiling and never makes money fails S3-C1 and S3-C3, and that is a real and anticipated way for Attempt 2 to fail.

disclosed_costs_of_the_architecture: Sell-side regulatory fees in SE100-CFG-2001 round UP to the cent, so a sale costs about two cents regardless of size. On a 95%-of-equity position that is roughly 2 bps; on a 50% position roughly 4 bps; on a 12.5% position roughly 16 bps. Lowering exposure therefore RAISES cost per unit of exposure. RA1 pays this drag on every trade and it is not modelled away.

RA1-1 halves exposure, so it also roughly halves the strategy's participation in the returns that made every Attempt 1 candidate profitable. Attempt 2's research question is precisely whether what remains is still meaningful after costs.
RA1-1 applies to a defensive Treasury leg as well, reducing its carry contribution.
RA1-4 forces an exit and a later re-entry on any position held to its horizon; with RA1-7 and RA1-6 that costs at least six sessions out of the market and two round-trip cost charges per cycle.
RA1-6 keeps the account in cash for five decision sessions after every risk exit, forgoing any recovery that occurs inside that window.

admissible_candidate_exists.across_candidates: DISJUNCTIVE. One admissible candidate is enough to pass Gate 3.

per_condition_rollup_is_not_the_gate.rule: A per-condition rollup row aggregates SATISFACTION across candidates and therefore means only 'at least one candidate satisfied this condition'. It is not evidence that any candidate satisfied all of them, and it settles nothing on its own.

per_condition_rollup_is_not_the_gate.decisive_row: The conditions table must carry the admissible_candidate_exists row, and that row alone decides the gate. A conditions table that omits it is misleading and is not an acceptable deliverable.

may_a_result_be_rerun_after_a_valid_comp.rule: Once a variant has completed a valid run over its full declared window under the sealed cost model, that result is the result. It is not re-run, not re-seeded, not re-ordered, and not recomputed in the hope of a different number. There is nothing to re-seed: SE100-CFG-3003 declares random_seeds null and every rule is deterministic, so a re-run of an unchanged variant must reproduce byte-identical output. A re-run that produced a DIFFERENT number would be a determinism defect and a blocker, not a better result.

when_a_rerun_is_required: A run that did not reach the development window end is NOT_RUN, not a result, and is re-run in full.

denominators_and_universes_of_measuremen.note: Restated from SE100-CFG-3002 for a reader, and enforced from that file. Nothing here is a new rule.
denominators_and_universes_of_measuremen.total_return: final equity divided by starting equity, minus 1. Starting equity is the sealed USD 100.00. An equity curve with fewer than two points is NOT_EVALUABLE and fails.
denominators_and_universes_of_measuremen.max_drawdown: largest peak-to-trough decline of the DAILY CLOSING equity curve, expressed as a non-negative fraction of the RUNNING PEAK. Session-close granularity; the project holds no intraday data and none is imputed.
denominators_and_universes_of_measuremen.profit_factor: gross profit divided by gross loss over CLOSED trades only. Trade P&L is exit cash plus dividends received while held, minus entry cash, with both legs' costs inside. Open positions at window end are excluded from the numerator and the denominator alike.
denominators_and_universes_of_measuremen.closed_trades: count of CLOSED round trips. Open positions at window end are not counted.
denominators_and_universes_of_measuremen.best_trade_removal: a multiplicative equity reconstruction over closed trades in order, from E[0] = 100.00 with E[i] = E[i-1] + pnl[i] and r[i] = E[i]/E[i-1]. Realised return is the product of all r[i] minus 1; the removed-trade return is the product over i not equal to j minus 1.
denominators_and_universes_of_measuremen.concentration: single-instrument closed-trade P&L divided by TOTAL closed-trade P&L, evaluated only when the total is strictly positive.
denominators_and_universes_of_measuremen.neighbour_stability: the SIGN of net return of each of the four neighbours, compared to the sign of the primary's net return. Magnitudes are irrelevant to the condition and zero matches nothing.

evidence: SE100-GOV-0001 section 11, lines 290-291: 'A change that affects universe, timing, cost, signal, parameter range, metric, threshold, or data partition is material.' and 'A material change after seeing validation results creates a new candidate and restarts at Gate 3.' items: Attempt 1's results are known to the researcher who wrote this file. This is an adaptive second attempt at Gate 3, not an independent first look.
All six Attempt 1 candidates breached the 15% maximum-drawdown ceiling. Some also failed the closed-trade-count floor, the profit-concentration condition, and the best-trade-removal condition.

The development data are no longer pristine with respect to at least the broad fact that the first candidate set produced excessive drawdown, and with respect to the per-candidate closed-trade counts recorded above. Attempt 2's design is conditioned on those facts.
Researcher degrees of freedom are higher in Attempt 2 than in Attempt 1, and false-discovery risk is correspondingly higher, because the design space was narrowed using an observed outcome.
The total experiment count for any later statistical interpretation is the cumulative count across both attempts, not Attempt 2's count alone. See cumulative_experiment_count.

No Attempt 2 result may be described as independent confirmation of anything merely because the code that produced it is new. The candidates share development data, a researcher, and a known prior outcome with Attempt 1.

Three of the three Attempt 2 candidates hold the entry and exit signal in the same rule FORM as a rejected Attempt 1 candidate. That is deliberate - the research question is about risk structure, so the return source is held fixed and the risk architecture is varied - and it means Attempt 2 is a second look at the same signals on the same data, not a new hypothesis about what predicts returns.
Validation-window and holdout-window protections are unchanged by this attempt. The validation window remains LOCKED and the holdout window remains SEALED.
A passing development result authorises only the next frozen evaluation step. It is not evidence of a trading edge, and it is not a claim about any future period.

This adaptation is not concealed behind a new strategy identifier. Each candidate id carries the RA1 suffix naming the shared risk architecture, and each candidate block states in distinction_from_attempt_1 exactly which rejected Attempt 1 candidate it shares its signal form with.

cumulative_experiment_count.binding_number_for_interpretation: 9 candidates and 45 gating variants against the same development window. Any later statistical statement about Gate 3 evidence uses the cumulative figure, not Attempt 2's figure.

cumulative_experiment_count_full.distinct_signal_forms: Attempt 2 introduces no new signal form. evidence.multiple_comparisons_disclosure: Three candidates are tested against the same development data that six candidates were already tested against, by a researcher who knows how those six failed. A per-candidate criterion is not a family-wise one, and the probability that at least one of nine specifications passes by chance exceeds the probability that any single pre-specified one does. Because the Attempt 2 design space was narrowed by an observed Attempt 1 outcome, the effective search is wider than nine independent draws and cannot be bounded by counting runs. Nothing in this attempt corrects for it numerically. The correction the constitution relies on is that an admitted candidate must still survive Gate 4 robustness, Gate 5's single sealed holdout read, and the duration-based paper and shadow gates. Attempt 2 weakens none of those and earns no relief from any of them.

grid_invariant.purpose: Each candidate declares a permitted_parameter_grid. This field states exactly what that grid means, once, so that three per-candidate prose notes cannot drift into three different rules and so that the invariant is machine-checkable.
invariant: For every key present in a candidate's permitted_parameter_grid, the declared value list is exactly the set formed by that candidate's primary value for the key together with every value the four declared neighbours give that key. Nothing else is permitted for that key.
Every key that at least one declared neighbour varies is present in the grid. A neighbour cannot vary a parameter the grid does not admit.
A key whose list holds a single value is a PIN, not a search axis: it records that the parameter exists, is fixed, and is deliberately not probed by any neighbour of this candidate.
grid_invariant.the_grid_is_not_the_full_parameter_set: The grid enumerates only the parameters this candidate's neighbours touch, plus any pin it names explicitly. Parameters of the primary that no neighbour varies and that the grid does not pin - max_hold, reentry_delay, ladder_rungs, vol_floor_fraction - are single-valued by their appearance in the primary parameterisation and are not restated in the grid. They are no less fixed for being absent from it.
grid_invariant.no_search: No search, sweep, or optimisation over any grid is performed at any point. The grid is a declared boundary on what could legitimately be run, and the runs that are actually run are the primary and its four neighbours - five per candidate, fifteen in total. A value inside the grid is not thereby authorised as an additional run.
grid_invariant.why_declare_a_boundary_that_is_not_searc: So that a later session cannot run a sixth variant, find it inside a broad grid, and call it pre-registered. The grid is deliberately narrower than Attempt 1's, which listed values no variant used.

evidence.no_retuning_rule: No parameter value, threshold, lookback, exposure fraction, volatility target, loss limit, holding period, re-entry delay, ladder rung, universe, or rule in this file may be changed for any reason once this file is sealed. A neighbour is never promoted to primary. A primary is never revised because a neighbour did better. No candidate is re-run at a different parameterisation. Under constitution section 11 any such change is material and creates a NEW candidate that restarts at Gate 3 under a NEW pre-registration; it does not repair a candidate declared here. Safety thresholds may be TIGHTENED without promoting a failed strategy, per section 11, but any such tightening must be versioned and may not be applied to a candidate whose result is already known.

iteration_budget.runs_per_candidate: one primary run plus four robustness-neighbour runs, plus one non-gating stressed-cost run of the primary
iteration_budget.meaning: Each candidate is run once at its primary parameterisation. No parameter is changed, no rule is amended, no symbol is added or removed, and no candidate is re-run after any result is seen. A candidate that fails is reported as failed. Constitution section 11: a change to universe, timing, cost, signal, parameter range, metric, threshold, or data partition is material, and a material change creates a NEW candidate that restarts at Gate 3 - it does not repair this one.
iteration_budget.neighbour_runs_are_not_iterations: The four neighbour runs per candidate exist solely to evaluate S3-C7 on the sign of net return. They are never used to select a parameterisation, are never promoted to primary, and their metrics other than the sign of net return are reported but carry no gate weight.
iteration_budget.stress_runs_are_not_iterations: The three stressed-cost runs are diagnostics required by constitution section 7. They are non-gating at Gate 3 and cannot admit or reject any candidate. See cost_stress_treatment.

may_a_result_be_rerun_after_a_valid_comp.rule: Once a variant has completed a valid run over its full declared window under the sealed cost model, that result is the result. It is not re-run, not re-seeded, not re-ordered, and not recomputed in the hope of a different number. There is nothing to re-seed: SE100-CFG-3003 declares random_seeds null and every rule is deterministic, so a re-run of an unchanged variant must reproduce byte-identical output. A re-run that produced a DIFFERENT number would be a determinism defect and a blocker, not a better result.

when_a_rerun_is_required: A run that did not reach the development window end is NOT_RUN, not a result, and is re-run in full.

A software defect discovered after a result exists INVALIDATES that result per constitution section 10. The result is recorded as INVALIDATED, the fix is recorded, and ALL affected runs are re-run in full.
rerun_policy.prohibited: Selectively re-running only the variants whose numbers were disliked, extending a partial run rather than re-running it, or patching a completed result.
rerun_policy.no_specification_change_ever_follows_a_r: A change to SE100-CFG-3003 after any Attempt 2 result exists creates a new candidate under a new pre-registration and restarts at Gate 3. It never repairs a candidate declared for this attempt.
